title: Restricted augmentation is a K-injective resolution
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $K$ a bounded-below cochain complex of abelian sheaves on its small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $T$ an étale termwise hypercohomology presentation of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. Let $q$ be any integer. The concrete augmentation $a_q:\sigma_{\ge q}K\to R_q$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-restricted-augmentation] is a quasi-isomorphism, and $R_q$ is K-injective.

source.place: Proof remark (3) and finite-diagonal comparison; Tag 0133, augmented-total quasi-isomorphism

proof.text: Restrict T.a to retained rows. Its rows are the original resolutions conjugated by truncation component isomorphisms, and omitted rows are zero. Terms stay injective and the bicomplex vanishes below q. Apply cartanEilenberg_total_resolution to this bounded-below stupid truncation. Its degree-zero summand formula identifies its augmentation with a_q degreewise. Hence a_q is a quasi-isomorphism and R_q is K-injective, also for empty diagonals and negative q.
